title: The AI-First Platform the Disaggregated Semiconductor Industry Needs
gist: At SEMICON West 2026 and CONNECT, PDF Solutions' Kimon Michaels argued that advanced packaging and a disaggregated, low-trust supply chain make an AI-first, cross-company data platform unavoidable, and launched Exensio Aurora (FUSE compute engine, ~25x faster claims, agentic workflows, secure feed-forward via secureWISE/Cimetrix/Sapience). The author notes the speed figures are vendor benchmarks and the real edge goes to whoever moves data and models across company boundaries securely.

insights.claim: Packaging now drives leading-edge semiconductor innovation, with manufacturing spread across companies and continents and the front-end/back-end boundary blurring, making AI a requirement rather than a nice-to-have, according to PDF Solutions' Kimon Michaels.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Value in semis is migrating to packaging and cross-company data — favors packaging and manufacturing-analytics vendors.
insights.locator: Michaels’ premise is easy to state

insights.claim: Because 2D geometric scaling has slowed and the reticle caps die size, the industry is moving to system-technology co-optimization: disaggregating systems into chiplets and recombining them via heterogeneous integration.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Chiplet/heterogeneous integration is the next scaling vector; supports advanced-packaging capacity and tooling.

insights.claim: Advanced packaging is expected to grow 26% going forward, driven today by AI accelerators and CPUs, with broader chiplet adoption expected to accelerate that growth.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: A 26% growth outlook supports OSAT, packaging equipment and related data-tool demand.
insights.locator: Advanced packaging is expected to grow at 26%

insights.claim: Qualcomm reported that its manufacturing data grew 600% since 2022, illustrating the data explosion from 3D-integrated packaging.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Exploding fab/test data volumes expand the addressable market for semiconductor data platforms.
insights.locator: Michaels recalled that at PDF’s 2025 Users Conference

insights.claim: Advanced semiconductor parts can carry 1 million to 10 million parameters across tens of test insertions, producing extremely wide but shallow, shifting data that tools built for tall, narrow business data handle poorly.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Generic BI/data-warehouse tools are structurally ill-suited to semi test data, creating a moat for specialized vendors.
insights.locator: The shape of the data matters

insights.claim: Simply collecting more of the same manufacturing data rarely helps AI; what matters is data that reveals relationships and cause and effect, reaching further across the supply chain.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Evaluate fab-AI vendors on cross-domain data linkage, not raw data volume.
insights.quote: Just collecting more of the data you already have generally doesn’t move the needle much

insights.claim: PDF Solutions' Exensio Aurora, announced September 9, 2026 and first shown at CONNECT on October 15–16, is built on five pillars atop the Exensio Manufacturing Data House: Scalable Analytics, Enterprise MLOps, Agentic, AI-First Interactivity and Edge Deployments.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: New product cycle for PDF Solutions; adoption pace is a revenue catalyst to track.
insights.locator: Exensio Aurora: five pillars on one data house

insights.claim: PDF Solutions built FUSE, a new distributed compute engine designed from scratch because it says no existing distributed engine supports the specificity of semiconductor data, claiming roughly 25x faster performance at the same cost or energy.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: A proprietary semi-specific compute engine could deepen PDF's differentiation if benchmarks hold.
insights.quote: no distributed computation engine supports the specificity of semiconductor data.

insights.claim: PDF Solutions' benchmarks claim Exensio Aurora is 18–40x faster on wide-data egress (25K–250K columns), 12–16x faster than prior Exensio at cost parity, makes 1M-column × 60K-row compute feasible, and loads and summarizes 2M columns × 60K rows (1,200 wafers) in about 10 minutes at a large foundry.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Strong claimed gains, but they are vendor figures — watch early-adopter customer validation.
insights.locator: In his CONNECT keynote, Michaels broke the gain down

insights.claim: The author cautions that Exensio Aurora's speed figures are PDF Solutions' own vendor benchmarks and that independent customer data and early-adopter results will tell the fuller story.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Discount headline benchmark claims until field data arrives.
insights.quote: As with any vendor benchmark, independent customer data will tell the fuller story.

insights.claim: Exensio StudioAI is pitched to train and serve tens of thousands of models across an enterprise with bring-your-own-model support and Kubernetes deployment, reflecting that shipping and monitoring models in production is harder than building them.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: MLOps at fab scale is a key differentiator for manufacturing AI platforms.
insights.quote: Building a model is the easy part.

insights.claim: Exensio Aurora ships first as six solution bundles (Scalable Analytics, Scalable Data APIs, Manufacturing Data House, Automated Analytics, StudioAI, Advanced Feed Forward) through an early-adopter program.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Early-adopter gating means revenue impact is back-loaded; track conversion to general availability.
insights.locator: What ships, and what it means

themes.theme: Agentic AI over multiple data houses

insights.claim: Kimon Michaels predicts that within five years user interfaces will not matter; what will matter is whether manufacturing data platforms expose what AI agents need to act on data across multiple data houses such as PLM, MES and design data.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Shifts competition in fab software from UI/dashboards to agent-accessible APIs and interoperability.
insights.quote: Five years from now, no one is going to care about the user interface,

insights.claim: In Exensio Aurora, workflows act as the system language — rules, ML pipelines and batch analytics are all workflows that can be built from natural language via an LLM, encode guardrails against hallucination and serve as long-term memory, with an orchestrator LLM hosting PDF, public and customer models side by side.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: A model-agnostic orchestration approach reduces lock-in concerns for customers bringing their own models.
insights.locator: In Aurora, workflows serve as the system language

insights.claim: Fabless chipmakers like Marvell or Broadcom never have their advanced chips in a factory bearing their name; 3D-integrated products pass through foundries, multiple OSATs, suppliers and system makers, with traceability getting harder at each step.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Fabless leaders depend on cross-company data flows they don't control — a structural opportunity for secure data-exchange vendors.
insights.quote: that chip is never in a factory with your name on it.

insights.claim: Most cross-company semiconductor collaboration still runs on email and phone calls, which is manual, unstructured and breaking down under 3D-integration complexity, because the industry is not built on trust.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: The gap between practice and need is large — a long runway for secure supply-chain data platforms.
insights.quote: We are not an industry built on trust.
insights.locator: Today, he observed, most cross-company collaboration

insights.claim: PDF Solutions' supply-chain stack combines the secureWISE remote-connectivity network, Cimetrix for equipment integration at the edge, and the Sapience Manufacturing Hub for ERP and enterprise links.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: PDF's acquired assets give it a full-chain connectivity position competitors may lack.

insights.claim: The payoff of cross-company data exchange is closed-loop feed-forward of data and AI models: collecting upstream data automatically, transforming it into model inputs, delivering it on each step's time constants, applying models at package sort or test, and returning results to the originating database.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Feed-forward test optimization improves OEE and can avoid burn-in — tangible ROI drivers for fabs and OSATs.

insights.claim: With chiplets, known good die is no longer sufficient; chiplet matching and chiplet–package interaction determine whether the finished part works, so avoiding scrap of $10,000–$20,000 finished parts justifies upstream data use.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: High finished-part values in AI packages raise the ROI of upstream screening and feed-forward analytics.
insights.quote: You can’t throw out a $10,000 or $20,000 part at the end if you can avoid it.

insights.claim: A former Department of Commerce supply-chain policy official distinguished data sharing from secure data exchange and predicted resistance to sharing enterprise data with AI vendors, as happened when EDA moved to the cloud.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Data-sovereignty concerns may slow cross-company AI adoption; gatekeeping platforms that secure agents and data could capture value.
insights.quote: because ultimately data is gold that people monetize.

insights.claim: Kimon Michaels argues cross-company semiconductor data exchange must enforce permissions that travel with the data, role-based access control, auditable logs and expiring access, and must be decentralized because no one party controls the industry.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Decentralized, permission-aware architectures favor neutral platforms over any single foundry-controlled system.
insights.quote: because no one party controls our industry.

insights.claim: In fabless–foundry relationships the foundry is a contract manufacturer, and the industry has not collectively worked out how sharing data beyond product qualification could affect future acceptance — a business-model obstacle larger than the technology.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Commercial terms, not tech, may be the binding constraint on supply-chain AI adoption.
insights.quote: is not something we have thought through collectively as an industry.
insights.locator: Michaels agreed that the issue goes beyond

insights.claim: The author concludes that because Moore's Law economics now run through the package and the package runs through companies that do not fully trust each other, the competitive edge in yield, quality and performance goes to whoever moves data and models across company boundaries securely with little human intervention.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Back players enabling secure cross-company data/model flow as packaging becomes the economic center of semis.
insights.locator: The technical claims will be judged in the field
